title: School
label: ch:ml-school
canDo: I can name a school and what happens in it — the lesson, the exam, and the marks.

payoff.summary: From cold: four school words, the three places they came from, and which one changes under a case ending.
payoff.note: FOUR NEW WORDS, AND THE POINT'S NOTE WAS PARTLY STALE. It said 'none of paLLikkoodam, paadam or pareeksha is taught', which is true of those three words and leaves out that the DOMAIN already has anchors: ML-C48-teacher (1290) owns adhyaapakan and ML-C48-student (1300) owns vidyaarthi. So the learner has had the PEOPLE since 1290 with nothing around them, and this chapter supplies the place, the thing taught in it, the test of it and the number at the end. That framing is the chapter's spine and it came out of verifying the note rather than scoping from it. A GLYPH CLAIM WAS CHECKED AGAINST DATA AND AGAINST THE FONT, NOT AGAINST A NOTE. pareeksha needs the ksha conjunct, and ML-A1-SCR-12's note lists 'sha (14)' among nine characters the corpus never teaches -- which would have made this word add script debt. It does not: ML-S121-letter-ssa (471) TEACHES the retroflex sha at U+0D37, and SCR-12's 'sha' is the OTHER sibilant, U+0D36, which really is untaught and which 12 distinct TOKENS in headword position need (sari, pashu, aakaasham among them) across 15 headword fields -- and the FIRST DRAFT EXPLAINED THAT GAP BACKWARDS, saying it came from shani and vRshchikam sitting inside multi-word headwords. A token inside a multi-word headword contributes ONE token and ONE field, so multi-word headwords cannot produce the discrepancy at all. The whole three-field gap is shubha, which occupies FOUR headword fields (ML-C25-shubha-rathri, ML-C30-shubha-sayaahnam, ML-C31-shubha-madhyaahnam, ML-C31-afternoon-convergence); every other token sits in exactly one. The variable is a token REPEATED ACROSS SIBLING HEADWORDS. SCR-12's own '14' is a third number nobody has re-derived. Filed as HL-C407; not widened into here. Separately paaThaM needs U+0D20, a character NO headword in the corpus has ever used, so the NotoSansMalayalam cmap was read directly before the word was committed to -- present -- which is what lessons.d means by 'a character no book has rendered before is invisible to every local gate'. ROMANIZATIONS ARE COPIED FROM NAMED WITNESSES, NEVER GUESSED: ksha -> ksa from six unanimous headwords (ML-C09, ML-C49, ML-C53, ML-C63, ML-C65, ML-C92), with apEksha fixing the word-final -ksa; the chillu r before a consonant -> r from seven (sharkkara, cherkkuka, karshakan, bharttaavu, karkkatakam, tiirccayaayum, vidyaarthi). Only ThaM is DERIVED rather than copied, because U+0D20 has no witness at all: ta is t, and every aspirate in this corpus carries an h (bha -> bh, dha -> dh), so Tha -> Th. THE TWO SANSKRIT WORDS DELIBERATELY DISAGREE. paaThaM ends in the anusvara and gives way to -tth- under a case ending, exactly as HL-C400 narrowed that rule to say; pareeksha ends in a and does not. Same chapter, same subject, same source language, different endings -- and the chapter says outright that the ENDING decides, not the meaning. That is a revisit of ML-GRAMMAR-C83-OBLIQUE-AM-01 on a word that earns it, rather than a restatement. THE ETYMOLOGY IS GIVEN IN ROMANIZATION ONLY. paLLikkooTaM is palli plus kooTaM, and neither part is a taught headword; naming them in SCRIPT would introduce two unowned tokens, which is the trap lessons.d records as 'the parts a lesson names to explain a word are forward references too'. They are given as palli and kooTaM, the way ML-C10-azhcha gives its Tamil comparisons. The historical claim is hedged to what is checkable about MODERN Malayalam -- palli is the word for a mosque or a church, kooTaM is a hall -- with the why offered as the traditional account rather than asserted. THE FULL SUITE CAUGHT WHAT TWELVE GATES DID NOT, for the second chapter running: script-closure.test.ts pins malayalam at neverTaughtGlyphs === 0 and paaThaM broke it. That pin is a STRONGER claim than SCR-12's note suggests -- U+0D36 counts as taught by that metric because it sits inside another letter lesson's example words, the understatement lessons.d already records -- while U+0D20 appears NOWHERE, not in a headword and not as an example. The fix is ML-S147-letter-ttha at sequence 3725, taught BETWEEN the school and the lesson that needs it, because closure is measured in READING ORDER and a letter taught late retires nothing. Teaching it beat the alternatives: padding an existing letter lesson's examples with the character would have moved the number without teaching anybody anything, and dropping paaThaM would have cost the point its best word. U+0D20 is U+0D1F with a breath after it, so it pairs naturally. THE DRAFT OF THAT LESSON CLAIMED MORE AND WAS WRONG: it called the character 'the only letter in the book that arrives with no history', which TEN merged script lessons contradict in identical words -- ML-S07, ML-S110, ML-S111, ML-S116, ML-S125, ML-S127, ML-S131, ML-S141, ML-S143 and ML-S144 each say of their own character that 'it has not been on a page yet: it arrives with the word on the next one'. Arriving with the word that needs it is this corpus's NORMAL way of introducing a letter. The lesson now uses that same house sentence. What is distinctive about U+0D20 is a fact about the METRIC, not about the reader, and it belongs in the record rather than in a lesson. Caught by reading, not by any gate, and it is the same shape as every other defect this run: a flattering universal in generalising prose.
